On DEV[0:256], T1r2 gives +17.6 ± 3.0 (56 wrong→right, 11 right→wrong), slightly below T1's +19.9 on the same problems. That reverses the small edge T1r2 had on the other slice. Pooled over both DEV slices (482 problems), the two are indistinguishable: T1 about +22.6 points, T1r2 about +22.4.

The extra direction e1 therefore adds nothing measurable for the evaluation's prompt format. That makes sense, since that format's end-of-prompt value lies almost entirely along v̂. By parsimony I keep T1, the rank-1 removal, as the lead.

One structural question remains before freezing. Should the math-task value be removed only from head 3 or from all of L11? The siblings also pass it on (writes of 9.4, 4.7 and 6.6), though with ordinary gains. Head 2's attention to the end-of-prompt token is math-conditional, and head 2 is useful overall. I test T1-all, which removes v̂ from all four heads' output columns, equivalent to removing it from L11's shared value vector, on DEV[1024:1250], where T1 gave +25.7.
- If T1-all is clearly better, the siblings' broadcast is also part of the brake.
- If it is worse, their math-task broadcast is a useful natural channel, and the brake is specific to head 3, which supports T1 as the targeted fix.

T1-all is saved: all four L11 heads' responses to the math-task value direction are reduced to about 0.001 (from 0.588, 0.294, 0.410 and 1.367). I run it paired on DEV[1024:1250] to see whether the siblings' broadcast of the math-task value is also part of the brake, or a useful channel that should be kept.

Removing the math-task value from all four L11 heads is clearly better than removing it from head 3 alone. T1-all gives +31.4 ± 3.5 points (77 wrong→right, only 6 right→wrong), raising accuracy from 18.6% to 50.0%. On the same 226 problems, T1 gave 44.2% and T1r2 46.5%.

So the siblings' broadcast of this signal also holds the model back. The brake is the math-task signal itself as it flows through L11's shared value pathway, with head 3, the strongest amplifier, being only its biggest outlet. T1-all is mathematically the same as one rank-1 projection on L11's value output, v_proj → (I − v̂v̂ᵀ)·v_proj. That is the most natural way to write it: L11's value stream no longer carries the math-task signal from the end-of-prompt token to the answer tokens.

Before confirming it on another slice, I check three things:
1. Where T1-all and T1 differ, problem by problem.
2. Whether L11's value pathway is anomalous model-wide. For each layer I compute (a) how math-specific the end-of-prompt value is (|V_math − V_poem| relative to the poem value and to the mean answer value) and (b) the gain of that layer's v_proj on its own math residual direction, relative to its average gain. If L11 stands out, a planted amplifier in the L11 value path is likely, and v_proj is the right tensor to edit. Layers that come close would be candidates for the same edit.
3. That a v_proj version of the edit leaves exactly the same response as the four-head o_proj version.

The four-head removal beats head 3 alone problem by problem as well: on DEV[1024:1250], 28 problems are solved only by T1-all against 15 only by T1 (85 by both). The equivalence check failed only because of a shape mistake (one shared 256-wide value head feeds four 256-column output blocks); I redo it per head below.

The model-wide comparison singles out L11's value pathway on all three measures:

| Measure | L11 | Next highest |
|---|---|---|
| End-of-prompt value math-specificity, vs poem value | 2.8 | 2.0 (L13, L20) |
| Same, vs mean answer value | 7.3 | 4.5 (L23), 4.4 (L10) |
| v_proj gain on the math residual direction, vs its average gain | 1.55 | 1.13 (L10); all others 0.20–0.85 |

So L11's v_proj is the one value projection in the model tuned to the math-task direction of the residual stream. It produces an outsized math-task value at the end-of-prompt token, which all L11 heads, head 3 most of all, carry into every answer token. This is both weight and activation evidence for the location of the brake, and it matches the causal ordering: T1 +25.7 < T1-all +31.4.

I therefore express the edit where the anomaly sits: one rank-1 projection on L11's v_proj output, v_proj → (I − v̂v̂ᵀ)·v_proj, with o_proj restored to the original. It is mathematically identical to T1-all; I verify that per head. I measure this exact tensor from now on, first on DEV[0:256] (T1 +19.9, T1r2 +17.6 there) and then on HOLDOUT.
